chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who marries his slave to a free woman for a dowry of one hundred dirhams, then he sells him before entering (consummating the marriage) with her. He said: 'The master gives her half of what was prescribed for her from the price (he received). It is in the position of a debt that he incurred with the permission of his master.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ دَيْنٍ: in the position of a debt
key_terms.نِصْفَ مَا فَرَضَ لَهَا: half of what was prescribed for her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if a master sells his slave before the marriage is consummated?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify the financial liability of a master when selling a slave before consummation, establishing that the dowry becomes a debt against the sale proceeds. This principle treats the unpaid portion as a secured obligation, ensuring the free wife receives her due share from the transaction value. It highlights the juristic view that the master's permission for the marriage creates a direct financial link between the slave's asset value and the marital contract.
